before: Equation fallback text changes owners between paragraph shared text and standalone records during display conversion.
after: Durably marked atomic controls keep fallback descendants under one record owner in both inline and display shapes. Generated text records use an atomicText Y.Array of immutable whole values; the last live entry wins. Each writer withdraws only its own previous entries. Ordinary editable text keeps Y.Text. Private payload fields append immutable XML elements so fallback and payload retain the same concurrent winner through undo.
reason: Seed, write routing, and text field representation change for marked fallback records. Existing paragraph text, Y.Text, scalar replacement, and mutable payload-field undo histories cannot be reinterpreted as replacement histories. Atomic histories enforce existing maxChildren and maxTextLength limits. Private histories enforce the existing 10000-field limit per record, an 8 MiB combined value limit, and the existing per-payload byte limit. DOCX preparation compacts redundant plain fields in validated supported payloads before reseeding; opaque metadata and original JSON remain intact. Existing rooms require DOCX export and reseeding into separate rooms, with old clients excluded.
